A_target.statement:
Let $\map P l$ be a [[Definition:Propositional Function|property]] of finite lists.
Suppose $\map P {\sqbrk {} }$ holds and:
:$\forall x, \mathit {xs}: \map P {\mathit {xs} } \implies \map P {x :: \mathit {xs} }$
Then $\map P l$ holds for every finite list $l$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\map P n$ be a [[Definition:Propositional Function|propositional function]] on $\N$.
Suppose $\map P 0$ holds and:
:$\forall n: \map P n \implies \map P {n + 1}$
Then $\map P n$ holds for all $n \in \N$.

validity_conditions: Both types are freely generated by their constructors (a base constructor and a step constructor), so the induction principle is valid in each.
proof_plan: The constructors of $\N$ are $0$ and the [[Definition:Successor Mapping|successor]]; the constructors of lists are $\sqbrk {}$ and $::$.
Map the base case $0$ to $\sqbrk {}$, and the step $n \mapsto n + 1$ to $\mathit {xs} \mapsto x :: \mathit {xs}$.

Prove $\map P {\sqbrk {} }$, then prove the step over the constructor $::$.
Equivalently, apply the [[Principle of Mathematical Induction]] to $\map Q n$: "$\map P l$ holds for all lists of length $n$".

Hence list induction is the same plan instantiated on a different [[Definition:Inductive Type|inductive type]].
{{qed}}
